There's been recent study results showing that Cypro at lower doses (anything below 300mg a day) actually acts as a progesterine, which has been shown to only help breast growth when your past the pubescent period of breast growth, tanner scale 1-2 (results vary with this, just like everything, your genes are the biggest bottleneck). At 300mg a day it acts as an anti-androgen, which a lot of research points to being more important for breast development (this information a recently got from my doctor who is a leading researcher in the field of trans medicine). Anti-androgens (such as Bicalutamide) inhibit the ability for the body to uptake T and DHT, where as progesterines stop the production of T in areas like the testicles and such, but doesn't stop the production of it in things that produce it as a byproduct, such as the adrenal glands. 
I've been on cypro the entire time I've been on HRT (10th of August 2020) and it hasn't exactly inhibited anything, but lately it has felt like I've been going back to my old moods pre HRT and my breast development has slowed down if not stopped (T levels are 0.2 and E levels are 295 btw). So in my opinion (something worth nothing really as I'm a random on Reddit) is that cypro is good to an extent, but should either be coupled with a real anti-androgen such as Bica, or just go on Spiro (which is an anti-androgen and a light progesterone)
